rationale:
Response to the round-1 critique. I accept most of it and partly reject one point.

Evidence: 60 trials of the raced iteration-2 design (16 mm sensors, x = -0.04..+0.04 at 0.02 m pitch, y = 0.04, kp 2.5, kd 0.2, ki 0.2, base 1.6, body 0.18, mass 0.8) all went off track at progress 0.11 to 0.16, with one line-loss event each and max_error 0.061 to 0.068 m. rms_error stayed near 0.03 m and steering oscillation was low (0.07 to 0.16). The failures are at the excursion peak, so the robot is under-correcting there, not oscillating. Iteration 0 (kp 3.0, 12 mm sensors) failed the same way, so the failure has persisted across a range of gains. The data does not isolate the cause.

Accepted from the critique: (a) my draft's kp cut to 2.0 reduced effective steering gain without evidence, so I restore it. Effective gain per metre scales as kp/spacing. Iteration 2 gave about 125 per m (2.5/0.02). Keeping that with 0.03 m spacing needs kp near 3.75, so I use kp 3.5 as a slightly conservative match. (b) base_speed 1.2 cost too much progress, so I use 1.5, not 1.2. (c) The kd statement was wrong, and kd is now set explicitly to 0.3, a moderate value that avoids the unbounded 0.6 noise risk. (d) ki 0.02 is too small to cancel the fixed motor mismatch, so I raise it to 0.1 (integral maximum about 0.2 turn, roughly 70 PWM). (e) The draft's mass 0.7 kg, body_length 0.16 m and y 0.06 m changes had no evidence, so I restore mass 0.8, body_length 0.18 and y 0.04 to isolate the sensor and gain changes.

Rejected from the critique: I keep the wider span (-0.06..+0.06). The critique's gap concern is weak: a 16 mm footprint at 30 mm pitch leaves 14 mm gaps, which is less than the 25 mm tape width, so the tape always covers at least one sensor.

Changes relative to iteration 2, and why: sensor span widened and pitch raised to 0.03 m (line visible at larger offsets); kp 2.5 to 3.5 (matches iteration-2 effective gain); kd 0.2 to 0.3; ki 0.2 to 0.1; base_speed 1.6 to 1.5. Geometry other than the sensor array is as raced.

Hypotheses, not data: fewer line-loss events than iteration 2, max_error nearer 0.06 m, and progress above 0.16. Completion remains uncertain at 1.5 base speed. Main risk: the wider span flattens the signal near centre, which could raise rms_error. Test: compare progress, line_loss_events and max_error on the s-bend track against iteration 2 to see whether the span change alone helps.
